findings.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret — other sessions survive
findings.problem: change_password now writes only password_hash: `new_auth = current_settings.auth.model_copy(update={"password_hash": SecretStr(new_hash)})`. auth.session_secret is unchanged, so every cookie signed before the change still validates. middleware.py:146 and routes.py:1357 both call validate_session(cookie, auth.session_secret.get_secret_value()) — with the secret constant, previously-issued cookies keep authenticating for the full COOKIE_MAX_AGE window. The sibling reset flow at routes.py:1941 still rotates and documents this as invariant D-12, so the two password-mutation paths now disagree.
findings.fix_hint: restore the rotation: generate_session_secret() into the model_copy update alongside password_hash, and re-issue the acting user's cookie with sign_session under the new secret (mirror routes.py:1941-2010)
findings.why_it_matters: The primary reason a user changes a password is a suspected compromise. A stolen session cookie keeps working after the change, so the remediation the UI implies ("Password updated") does not actually happen.

findings.title: Acting user's session cookie is no longer re-issued after password change
findings.problem: The handler previously built a response, set a fresh triggarr_session cookie via sign_session(refreshed_username, new_session_secret), and returned it. It now returns templates.TemplateResponse directly with no Set-Cookie. This is only benign because the secret is also no longer rotated (bugs-001). If bugs-001 is fixed without also restoring this block, the acting user logs themselves out on the next request. The two removals are coupled and must be restored or kept removed together.
findings.fix_hint: restore the set_cookie block alongside the rotation; keep attributes mirroring login_post (max_age=COOKIE_MAX_AGE, httponly, samesite=lax, secure=is_secure_request(request))
findings.why_it_matters: Restoring rotation alone would evict the user who just changed their own password, turning a security fix into a lockout on an htmx partial response that cannot redirect to login cleanly.

findings.title: POST /settings/password no longer rotates session_secret so stale cookies stay valid
findings.problem: The diff removes session_secret rotation from POST /settings/password (change_password). Previously, changing your password also rotated auth.session_secret, which invalidates every existing signed session cookie (validate_session fails for all of them) — logging out all other devices/sessions. After this change, password change only updates password_hash; the session_secret is untouched, so any previously-issued session cookie (including one held by an attacker who compromised the account) remains valid and continues to authenticate after the change. The sibling route POST /reset/confirm (reset_confirm_post, lines 1937-2011) explicitly retains this exact rotation and documents it as a required invariant (D-12) with an H2 read-back guard enforcing it. The removed code in this diff carried identical comment language, so this is a direct, visible behavioral regression versus the still-present sibling implementation.
findings.fix_hint: Restore session_secret rotation in change_password, mirroring reset_confirm_post: generate a new_session_secret via generate_session_secret(), include it in the model_copy update alongside password_hash, and re-issue the acting user's own cookie with sign_session(username, new_session_secret) after persisting/reloading settings.
findings.why_it_matters: A stolen session cookie keeps authenticating after the password change the user made to evict it, while the sibling /reset/confirm route still rotates — only one of two routes was changed.

findings.title: Duplicated persist sequence in change_password and reset_confirm_post now silently diverges
findings.problem: change_password and reset_confirm_post now duplicate a divergent copy of the same persist sequence (model_copy -> _settings_to_dict -> run_in_executor(_atomic_toml_write) -> os.chmod 0o600 -> load_settings -> _sync_auth_state -> collect_secrets -> setup_logging). The duplication predates this diff (it is why reset_confirm_post's docstring pins itself to 'change_password lines 1468-1470'), but the diff makes the two copies silently disagree on a security-relevant step rather than being line-for-line parallel. This is the failure mode of copy-paste coupling maintained by comment reference: editing one copy leaves the other's docstring asserting a correspondence that no longer holds.
findings.fix_hint: Extract the shared 'persist auth mutation + reload + refresh redacting sink' sequence into one helper both routes call, so a change to the rotation policy is made once and cannot drift. This is a refactor-class observation, not a defect fix — separate it from the primary rotation-restoration fix.
findings.why_it_matters: Copy-paste coupling maintained only by comment references lets the two password-write paths drift on a security-relevant step without any automated signal.

findings.title: Password change no longer rotates session_secret — other devices' sessions survive
findings.problem: The diff removes session_secret rotation from POST /settings/password. Previously the secret was regenerated so every cookie signed with the old secret failed validate_session (triggarr/web/middleware.py:146), evicting all other devices. Now only auth.password_hash is written; auth.session_secret is unchanged, so every pre-change session cookie continues to validate for the full COOKIE_MAX_AGE window (30 days, triggarr/auth.py:11). This removes the security guarantee the endpoint's own docstring/tests describe: an attacker with a stolen session cookie is NOT logged out by the victim changing their password — the primary remediation a user has. Verified by running the suite: tests/test_auth_routes.py::test_change_password_rotates_session_secret_and_persists, ::test_change_password_reissues_acting_user_cookie, and ::test_change_password_evicts_other_device_session all FAIL on this working tree (3 failed, 5 passed).
findings.fix_hint: Restore generate_session_secret() into the model_copy update and re-issue the acting user's cookie, mirroring the still-intact reset_confirm_post path at routes.py:1941-2008.
findings.why_it_matters: Session-fixation remediation is gone: compromised cookies remain valid for 30 days after a password change, and three existing tests encoding that promise now fail, so the branch cannot ship green.

After this diff the two sibling paths no longer mirror each other: a token-based reset evicts other sessions, an authenticated password change does not. Any future maintainer reading the reset docstring's mirror claim will be misled, and the D-12/D-13 decision records now only hold on one of the two paths.

findings.title: Restore session revocation on password change
findings.problem: Updating only password_hash preserves the session signing secret. validate_session checks only the signature and age, and AuthMiddleware accepts that cookie without checking the password. Consequently, a stolen cookie remains usable after the owner changes their password, for up to its remaining 30-day lifetime. This also violates the explicit revocation requirement covered by existing password-change tests.
findings.fix_hint: Restore generation and persistence of a fresh session_secret alongside the password hash, and reissue the acting user's cookie under that secret.
findings.why_it_matters: A stolen cookie remains usable after the owner changes their password, for up to its remaining 30-day lifetime.
